summary: Earlier versions carried Medicaid pharmacy payment rules for 340B drugs and a pharmacy benefit manager report that named 340B. The text that became law does not name the program.
Would add rural emergency hospitals to the providers that can take part in 340B.
Among the things a Medicare Part D pharmacy benefit manager would have to report is a list of the drugs for which it, or an affiliate, had an arrangement with a 340B covered entity.
Would order an analysis that includes how far certain noncitizens receive drugs bought under 340B.

In its Medicaid pharmacy payment rules, would let a plan or pharmacy benefit manager pay a covered entity more than its cost for a 340B drug, up to what it would pay had the drug been bought outside the program, if the covered entity reports to the Secretary; what is reported would be published by state and by type of covered entity. It would also have Medicare Part D pharmacy benefit managers list the 340B drugs for which they had an arrangement with a covered entity.
Would bar a covered entity from using what it earns through 340B to pay for sex reassignment surgeries or hormone treatments for transgender individuals.
Names 340B among the programs whose claims count toward a test for what the bill calls a priority research drug.
Names 340B in a list of drug units that are counted apart when Medicare drug inflation rebates are worked out.
One section would require a covered entity to give each patient a 340B drug at no more than the price the entity paid for it, and have the Secretary publish what is paid and received for those drugs.
Would let 340B covered entities apply for grants to provide sexual health services to young people.

Would bar a drug maker from putting conditions on a covered entity's purchase of 340B drugs, such as limits on where the drugs are delivered or dispensed or a demand for claims data, and adds a paragraph on contract pharmacies.

A broad rewrite of the program. Its sections cover contract pharmacies, hospital eligibility and child sites, what patients pay, Medicaid duplicate discounts, reporting by covered entities, a claims data clearinghouse, fees, and equal treatment of covered entities by payers.

Two sections would add reporting for hospitals in 340B: yearly data on how they provide care for patients, to be published by the Department of Health and Human Services, and reports by disproportionate share hospitals on their low-income utilization rate.

Would have high-revenue tax-exempt hospital organizations that are covered entities report 340B figures on their tax return: the people given 340B drugs by type of insurance, what was paid for those drugs above the ceiling price, and what it cost to take part.
